plan.topic: Is semaglutide safe if your kidneys are already weaker? Safety outcomes by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial (Kidney International, Oct 20, 2026)
plan.angle: Before scripting, find and verify the Kidney International Oct 20, 2026 paper. If it can't be found, build the Short on what is confirmed: FLOW's main result (type 2 diabetes plus CKD, semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly versus placebo, primary kidney outcome 19% versus 23%, HR 0.76, median 3.4 years), the CJASN 2026 finding that kidney and survival benefits were consistent across eGFR and albuminuria levels, and, as a whole-trial result, fewer serious adverse events on semaglutide (49.6% versus 53.8%) but more stopping because of GI side effects at every eGFR level. Keep the title as a question with no 'safe' claim, e.g. 'Semaglutide With Weaker Kidneys: What the FLOW Trial Found'. Keep the eGFR/urine albumin check and dehydration actions, 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own', 'Not personal advice' and the full prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Semaglutide and Weaker Kidneys: What the FLOW Trial Found #shorts
plan.why: A fresh FLOW paper with little coverage on a common worry. The body-worry format works on YouTube (about 104) and is our top Instagram format (reach 112). Semaglutide-only is allowed because the evidence covers semaglutide only. | fact-check: FLOW is real: adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD, semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly versus placebo, 3,533 participants, median follow-up 3.4 years. Its main kidney result was HR 0.76 for the primary kidney composite. But I could not confirm a FLOW secondary analysis in Kidney International dated Oct 20, 2026. The CKD-severity analyses I could confirm are: (a) WCN25-1900 'Clinical and Safety Outcomes of Semaglutide by CKD Severity in the FLOW trial', an abstract in Kidney International Reports; (b) Tuttle et al. 2026, 'Kidney and Survival Outcomes with Semaglutide by CKD Severity in the FLOW Trial', CJASN, which covers efficacy, not detailed safety. What those sources report on safety: fewer serious adverse events on semaglutide than placebo overall (49.6% vs 53.8%), and more GI-related discontinuations on semaglutide across the full eGFR range. Don't write 'safe for weaker kidneys'. Write 'in this trial population, the safety results were broadly similar across kidney-function levels' only if the source says so. Give 1.0 mg only as the trial arm, never as advice. Semaglutide only, so no tirzepatide claims and no #Tirzepatide. The 'follow for more' ending is fine.

social.instagram_caption:
Type 2 diabetes and weaker kidneys? Here's what a big semaglutide trial found.

If you have type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, that question matters. Here's what the FLOW trial (3,533 adults, median 3.4 years) found:

• Semaglutide 1 mg weekly vs placebo: 19% vs 23% had kidney failure, kidney function falling by half or more, or kidney/heart-related death.
• A 2026 analysis found the kidney and survival benefits held across the kidney-function and urine-albumin levels studied, down to an eGFR of 25. Dialysis wasn't studied.
• Serious adverse events were less common on semaglutide: 49.6% vs 53.8%.
• The catch: more people stopped semaglutide than placebo because of stomach side effects like nausea, vomiting and diarrhea (4.5% vs 1.1%). The label warns dehydration from these can affect your kidneys, so if that happens, call your prescriber.

Ask your prescriber about eGFR and urine albumin checks. Save or share this if you or someone you love is managing diabetes and kidney health.

If you're managing type 2 diabetes alongside chronic kidney disease, you've probably wondered whether a medicine like semaglutide is still safe for you.

The FLOW trial compared semaglutide 1 mg weekly with placebo in 3,533 adults with both conditions over a median of 3.4 years. Kidney failure, a kidney function drop of half or more, or kidney/heart-related death happened in 19% of people on semaglutide versus 23% on placebo. A follow-up 2026 analysis found those benefits held across the kidney-function and urine-albumin levels studied, down to an eGFR of 25 (dialysis wasn't studied). Serious adverse events were also less common on semaglutide (49.6% vs 53.8%). The trade-off: more people stopped semaglutide than placebo due to stomach side effects like nausea, vomiting and diarrhea (4.5% vs 1.1%), and the label notes dehydration from these can affect your kidneys.

Worth asking your prescriber about eGFR and urine albumin checks. Save or share this if it helps.

factcheck.summary:
This Short passes: the facts are right and it's safe to publish. Before render, apply the minor fixes listed, starting with the word count.

**What I confirmed in the main FLOW paper and the 2026 kidney-journal follow-up:**
- 3,533 adults with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease, on semaglutide 1 mg weekly versus placebo.
- Kidney-function entry range eGFR 25–75, with raised urine albumin.
- Median follow-up 3.4 years.
- Main outcome 19% versus 23%. The definition in the script (kidney failure, kidney function halved or worse, kidney or heart-related death) matches the paper.
- Serious adverse events 49.6% versus 53.8%.
- Stopped for stomach side effects 4.5% versus 1.1%.
- The 2026 follow-up (Tuttle et al., Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology) exists. It reports that the kidney and survival benefits held across all the kidney-function and urine-albumin levels studied.

**Safety and supporting sources:**
- The current Ozempic label (209637s038) has a warning on acute kidney injury from dehydration.
- MedlinePlus covers telling your doctor about vomiting, diarrhea and dehydration.
- The NIDDK page (US kidney institute, NIH) covers urine albumin checks and the kidney blood test.
- The disclaimer, the prescriber line and the "don't stop or change your medicines" line are all there.
- No spoken call-to-action names another video, so there's no link risk.

**Minor issues:**
- The narration is about 186 words, over the 170-word limit for Shorts.
- Some on-screen text in s2, s3 and s4 is vaguer or broader than what's spoken.
- The MedlinePlus source year is out of date.

issues.problem: The narration is about 186 words including the disclaimer. The limit for Shorts is 170, and long Shorts also tend to get the densest music mixes.
issues.fix: Trim to 170 words or fewer with these swaps. s4 narration: "A twenty twenty-six analysis found the benefits held across the kidney-function and urine-albumin levels studied, down to E-G-F-R twenty-five. Dialysis wasn't studied." s6 narration: "The catch: more people stopped semaglutide for stomach side effects like nausea, vomiting and diarrhea: four point five versus one point one percent." s7 narration: "Ask about E-G-F-R and urine albumin checks. Dehydrated from vomiting or diarrhea? Call your prescriber." Keep the label line on screen.

issues.problem: "Big kidney decline" is vaguer than the spoken and trial definition (kidney function down 50% or more). It also doesn't name the drug or the placebo group, so a muted viewer can't tell what is being compared.
issues.fix: Kidney failure, kidney function halved or kidney/heart death: semaglutide 19% vs placebo 23% (median 3.4 yrs)

issues.problem: The card doesn't say what held. "eGFR 25+" also reads as open-ended, but the trial enrolled eGFR 25–75.
issues.fix: Kidney + survival benefits held across levels studied (eGFR 25–75)

issues.problem: The caption doesn't name the population, the drug arm or the comparator (the muted-viewer test).
issues.fix: FLOW: 3,533 adults, type 2 diabetes + CKD · semaglutide 1 mg vs placebo

issues.problem: The page now says it was last revised on 05/15/2026.

notes: At 7.0s and 9.9s, faint ghost text ('Semaglut...', 'Placebo') is visible bleeding through under the dark caption pill, matching the automated overlap findings.
Syringe characters are headless/faceless props with no title card context beyond the caption, feels thin.
Caption card at 17.5s reads 'OF THREE POINT' and is cut mid-number, ending on the word 'POINT' which is a banned trailing word.
'NINETEEN PERCENT' is spelled out as number words instead of a numeral, risking mismatch with the spoken stat.
Caption 'HAD KIDNEY FAILURE,' stands alone on its own card next to a kidney mascot — an alarming phrase isolated on screen, against the house style rule.
'TWENTY-THREE PERCENT.' is spelled out in words instead of '23%'.
A smiling heart next to 'kidney failure' messaging risks a tonal mismatch (happy mascot near a serious adverse outcome).
Small eGFR 75 / eGFR 50 tags render tiny and overlap the 'KIDNEY FUNCTION?' and 'ANALYSIS FOUND THE KIDNEY' captions (matches automated overlap findings at 32.85s and 35.36s).
Three kidney icons plus overlapping eGFR chips feel cluttered for a vertical frame.
Caption at 42.4s reads 'G F R' as spaced single letters instead of 'GFR', hard to parse at speed and against the no-spaced-letters rule.
At 45.1s a ghost tag 'Dialysis: not studied' is visible faintly behind the 'DIALYSIS WASN'T STUDIED.' caption pill (matches the overlap finding).
Frame is otherwise sparse: a question mark and one small kidney with a lot of empty space.
Caption 'VERSUS FIFTY-THREE POINT EIGHT.' spells the number out in words instead of showing '53.8%', inconsistent with the stat pill that already shows the numeral.
Top of frame shows an unfilled template strip: three grey boxes with dash placeholders, a leftover dashed placeholder shelf that should have been deleted before render.
Otherwise the queasy stomach mascot and caption are clear.

audio.soundNotes: Music already sits in the -12 to -15 dB window relative to voice, so left the overall level untouched. The two chip/callout shots (21.5s and 67.8s) and several transition moments had 5-9 overlapping SFX firing within 1-4 seconds (duplicate swoosh/whoosh/blip/tick pairs at identical timestamps); I dropped the redundant duplicates and thinned each cluster down to 2-4 sounds max. Several reveal accents (blip/ding/swell) during speech were sitting at -13 to -13.8 dB relative to voice, slightly hotter than the -14 to -20 dB speech target, so I pulled those gains down about 25-30%. The disclaimer beat ("Not personal advice") got extra thinning and lower gains to keep that moment calm and trustworthy rather than busy.
